insights.insight: SINGLE-NAME CONCENTRATION RULE: Never recommend more than one trade in the same sector or with >0.6 correlation. The worst trials (138, 161, 162) all involved correlated double-bets. If two semis score well, take only the highest-conviction one.

insights.insight: REGIME-FORCED PARTICIPATION: When regime is risk-on with confidence >55% AND appetite >65%, the algorithm MUST generate at least one long candidate. When stress >18 AND appetite <35, it MUST generate at least one short/defensive candidate. The current no-trade default on actionable days is the #1 performance leak.

insights.insight: RECLASSIFY 'RANGE-BOUND' DEFAULT: Add a secondary momentum-persistence check. If the last 3-4 days show consistent directional moves (e.g., 4 consecutive down days in Trial 167), override range-bound with directional-trending-down/up. Range-bound should only apply when there are genuine alternating up/down days with no trend.

insights.insight: SEMICONDUCTOR SECTOR PENALTY: Apply a -5 point penalty to all semi trades (LRCX, AMAT, SMH, NVDA, AMD) unless there is a company-specific catalyst (earnings, product launch, export ruling). Generic 'semi rotation' trades have a near-zero win rate in the sample.

insights.insight: BRIEFING-RECOMMENDATION ALIGNMENT CHECK: Add a hard rule that the briefing sentiment and trade direction must agree. Trial 162 briefing was bearish with short recs (aligned), but Trial 161 briefing was bullish with long recs that lost. The issue in 161 was that 'rotation' regime + bullish briefing + semi longs = contradictory signals. If regime says rotation and briefing says bullish, go long in the sector rotating INTO, not the one showing momentum.

insights.insight: Enforce maximum 1 trade per day — the algorithm's only consistent edge is concentrated single-name bets. When multiple candidates pass threshold, take only the highest-scoring one. Multi-trade days have 0% win rate in the sample.

insights.insight: Reduce marketAlignment weight from 18% to 12% and redistribute to technicalSetup and riskReward. In rotation and range-bound regimes (which dominate recent trials), market alignment is actively misleading because broad market direction doesn't predict individual stock moves.

insights.insight: Create a 'low-confidence regime' trade pathway: when regime confidence is below 45%, allow trades ONLY if the individual stock catalyst score is above 80 AND technical setup shows a clear breakout/breakdown with volume confirmation. Currently the algorithm goes silent when regime confidence is low, but some of the best individual stock setups occur precisely in uncertain macro environments.

insights.insight: Add a correlation filter: if recommending multiple trades, reject any pair with trailing 20-day correlation above 0.70. Trials 138 (MSFT+AMD), 161 (LRCX+SMH), and 162 (AMAT+SMH) all failed with highly correlated pairs that doubled down on the same directional bet.

insights.insight: Implement a regime-direction consistency check: if regime='rotation' and briefing='bullish', the algorithm should NOT take broad directional bets (long semis, long indices). Rotation regimes demand pair-trade logic or single-name relative strength plays. Add explicit guardrail: rotation regime → only allow trades in the sector showing relative inflow, not the sector showing outflow.
